messages:
Alex: Quick follow-up from the fanout-compression RFC — we need to pick a pragmatic default for schema-gate behavior before the sprint starts.
Maya: Do we have a short summary of the options?
Alex: TL;DR: 1) Strict schema-gate at ingress (reject/drop unknown attrs) 2) Lenient ingress + canonicalizer in pipeline 3) Compression transform that prunes unknowns but preserves a minimal provenance envelope. Each has cost/query tradeoffs.
Sanjay: Option 1 gives best query predictability but will block many edge SDK versions. Ops overhead to coordinate rollout is non-trivial.
Irene: Option 2 is safest for client compatibility, but increases storage and downstream enrichment cost. We need a stronger dedupe/compaction pass later.
Jess: Can we quantify cost delta roughly? e.g., +X% storage, +Y% ingest CPU for option 2 vs 3?
Alex: Prototype roughs: option 2 ~ +18% storage, +12% CPU; option 3 (compress at ingress) ~ +6% storage, +4% CPU but needs a small provenance cache which complicates fanout.
Luke: For chargeback, ingress compression loses some attribute lineage — hard to reconstruct which service added which attr. That affects tenant-level billing accuracy.
Sanjay: We could keep a tiny breadcrumb envelope (origin, sdk_version, attr_hash) to help attribution while trimming payload. Small win for query/chargeback.
Irene: Breadcrumbs sound reasonable. How big per event?
Alex: ~120 bytes avg. At 500M events/day that's ~60GB/day extra — not trivial. But we can TTL breadcrumbs (7d) and retain full lineage only for sampled events.
Jess: Hybrid: sampled full lineage retention + lightweight breadcrumb for all. Pragmatic. Any gotchas?
Maya: Risks: 1) queries needing full lineage for non-sampled events will fail. 2) SDK rollbacks where compression permanently drops fields unless canonicalizer can rehydrate.
Sanjay: For SDK churn, require a compat header in breadcrumb: "compat_v" so canonicalizer picks proper transform rules. Allows safe prune + later rehydrate.
Alex: Proposed decision: default to option 3 (ingress compression) + breadcrumb envelope {origin, sdk_v, attr_hash, compat_v} + 7d breadcrumb TTL + sampled full-lineage retention (tenant-configurable).
Irene: +1 if we add a migration playbook for SDK owners and an explicit deprecation window for attribute removal.
Luke: Note: chargeback queries should have a best-effort mode that falls back to sampled lineage and surface a warning tag in results.
Jess: I'll update the RFC follow-up doc with cost numbers and fallback guidance.
Alex: Next steps: Jess updates doc; Infra outfits a small metadata TTL tier for breadcrumbs; DevEx emails SDK owners about compat header and deprecation windows.
ops-bot: Reminder: schedule review meeting — /remind @eng-platform in 2 days to review updated RFC. :calendar:
Maya: Thanks all, I'll sync with DevEx on the email copy.
Alex: Closing thread — we'll land the decision in the RFC doc and track rollouts in the sprint board.
